engine.meaning: The policy is reproduced verbatim apart from spelling ("authorisation", "Travelling"), so every rule survives: "TDY travel is more than 12 hours long", "expires one year (26 pay periods)".
engine.sense: No Aussie terms were introduced, so none takes a wrong sense; only "authorisation" and "Travelling" respelt.
engine.authenticity: Nothing Australian beyond spelling; the prose is the US original: "You may request travel comp time when you are approved to travel for work".
engine.register: Untranslated: "When you reach the expiration date, you will forfeit the leave." Under the level-2 brief.
engine.tone: The original's formal HR tone, unchanged.

unharnessed.meaning: Every rule kept: "TDY travel is longer than 12 hours and needs a pre-approved authorisation in Concur", "travel ends when you check in at the hotel or get home", "runs out one year (26 pay periods) after you earn it".
unharnessed.sense: Plain swaps fit: "getting to and from work" for commuting, "work out the breakdown", "Once you hit the expiry date", "took off and landed".
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural plain Australian English: "Have a look at OPM's [Travel Comp Time Fact Sheet]", "Please get in touch with your Timekeeper", "expiry date".
unharnessed.register: A shade light even for level 2: casual plain English with "Have a look", "check out", "work out", "expiry", but nothing distinctively Aussie.
unharnessed.tone: Stays a clear, helpful HR page: "If you leave GSA, any unused travel comp time is lost."
unharnessed.flow: Smooth throughout: "Use the time zone where you departed from to work out elapsed time." (a small "where ... from" redundancy).
unharnessed.variety: "work out" three times ("to work out the breakdown", "For working out", "to work out elapsed time"); otherwise little slang to vary.
unharnessed.essence: Clearly the TTS comp-time policy, every section kept.

yarn.meaning: Every rule kept, with a helpful gloss: "travel comp time (time in lieu for travel)", "needs an authorisation approved beforehand in Concur", "expires one year (26 pay periods) after you earn it".
yarn.sense: Terms fit: "time in lieu" is the Australian workplace term for comp time, "normal working hours", "have a chat to your Timekeeper", "GSA staff".
yarn.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian HR page: "time in lieu for travel", "If you've got questions, have a chat to your Timekeeper or an HR Specialist at your agency."
yarn.register: Level 2: a light, natural touch with "time in lieu", "have a chat to", "staff"; no swearing.
yarn.tone: Clear, helpful HR tone kept: "If you leave GSA, any travel comp time you haven't used is forfeited."
yarn.flow: Smooth: "Travelling during your usual work day counts as normal hours, and that includes travelling from home to the airport."
yarn.variety: "normal" four times and "work out" twice; light touch otherwise varied.
yarn.essence: Clearly the TTS policy, every section kept.
